sections.title: Market Pulse: Tech Rally Boosts Indices Amidst Fed Hawkishness

items.headline: U.S. stocks concluded Friday's session predominantly higher, propelled by a robust rally in the technology sector.
items.summary: The market's positive momentum was largely driven by stronger-than-expected earnings reports from major tech firms, particularly NVIDIA's optimistic revenue forecast, which reignited investor confidence in the artificial intelligence boom. This occurred even as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh indicated potential future interest rate hikes to combat persistent inflation.

items.headline: NVIDIA Surges on Strong Earnings and AI Forecast
items.summary: Shares of semiconductor giant NVIDIA ($NVDA) jumped 8.7% after reporting second-quarter 2026 earnings that beat estimates and projecting robust revenue growth for fiscal 2028, largely driven by demand for artificial intelligence.

items.headline: Salesforce Soars on Q2 Beat and Upbeat Guidance
items.summary: Salesforce, Inc. ($CRM) shares surged 22.6% after the company exceeded both earnings and revenue estimates for its second quarter and raised its fiscal 2027 guidance.

items.headline: Elastic Jumps on Strong FQ1 Results and Raised Outlook
items.summary: Elastic ($ESTC) shares gained 19% after the search and observability software company reported strong fiscal Q1 results and subsequently raised its fiscal year 2027 outlook.

items.headline: PayPal Declines as Buyout Bid Reportedly Abandoned
items.summary: PayPal Holdings ($PYPL) fell 12.84% during the week ending August 28, with reports indicating that a potential $50 billion buyout bid from Advent and Stripe was abandoned.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Slides After Earnings
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) saw a decline of 10.28% following its earnings report, contributing to the broader negative performance in some technology stocks not benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Signals Potential Rate Hikes at Jackson Hole
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, indicating that inflation remains stubbornly high at 3.7% (PCE) and that the central bank might need to raise interest rates in the coming months. His remarks reinforced the Fed's commitment to achieving its 2% inflation target.

items.headline: Technology and Consumer Discretionary Lead Sectors; Industrials and Healthcare Lag
items.summary: The Information Technology sector was the top performer, gaining 3.2% for the day through the XLK ETF, with strong performance extending to communication services. Consumer discretionary also emerged as a leading sector, advancing 1.69% on Friday. In contrast, ten of the eleven S&P 500 sectors closed in negative territory on Thursday, with Industrials down 2.13% and Healthcare down 2.06% for the week.

items.headline: Jobless Claims Fall, Q2 GDP Unchanged, Consumer Sentiment Revised Up
items.summary: New jobless claims decreased by 4,000 to 203,000 for the week ending August 22, while continuing claims also fell. The U.S. Q2 GDP growth remained unrevised at 1.5%. Meanwhile, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for August was revised upward to 51.7.

items.headline: Strong Tech Earnings Continue to Drive Market Enthusiasm
items.summary: Beyond NVIDIA and Salesforce, other companies like Elastic ($ESTC) and Affirm Holdings ($AFRM) reported strong earnings, contributing to the overall positive sentiment in the tech sector. CrowdStrike ($CRWD) also delivered better-than-expected fiscal Q2 results, raising guidance amidst increasing demand for cybersecurity solutions related to AI risks.
